items.title_en: Houthi missile hits Saudi Aramco HQ building in Dhahran after Saudi strikes on Sanaa – Brent edges up to ~$106.40 in Asia
items.summary_en: Reuters: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was hit Tuesday evening (Saudi time), causing a limited fire and no casualties. A company source said a ballistic missile struck the office tower, damaging the top three floors. Earlier, the Saudi-led coalition hit the Sabah fuel depot outside Sanaa, Yemen; the Houthis threatened both Aramco's headquarters and a Riyadh refinery. Debris from an intercepted missile injured four people in Riyadh. President Trump spoke with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; the US has not joined the fighting directly. Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz closed since February, which makes the Bab el-Mandeb route even more important. Markets: Brent (BZ=F, Yahoo) $106.39 at 7:45 PM ET Oct 13 vs. a $105.69 settle; COMEX gold (GC=F) flat around $4,179–4,184 (6:00–7:45 PM ET). No CNBC story on the Aramco attack yet.
items.reason_en: Near term: geopolitical risk is a safe-haven tailwind for gold, but the bigger effect runs through oil – higher crude → hotter inflation → more reason for the Fed to hike → firmer dollar and yields → headwind for gold. The two forces offset, so gold barely moved overnight. Bigger picture: if the Houthis keep hitting Saudi oil infrastructure, crude can spike and pull rate-hike bets higher; if the US or Turkey gets drawn in and the war escalates, the safe-haven bid for gold should become clearer.

Số liệu CFTC cho thấy vị thế đặt cược USD tăng lên khoảng 36 tỷ USD trong tuần tới 7/10, từ 8,4 tỷ USD ba tuần trước. CME FedWatch: 81% khả năng Fed giữ lãi suất tháng 10. CFTC data show net dollar longs rose to about $36B in the week to Oct 7, from $8.4B three weeks earlier. CME FedWatch: 81% odds of an October hold. Kitco: after Monday's close spot gold was around $4,168.90/oz (−0.59%), silver $60.12 (−0.96%); the market sees about 87.7% odds of at least one Fed hike by December.
items.reason_en: A strong dollar makes gold pricier for non-US buyers and goes hand in hand with Fed tightening bets → downside pressure. Kitco: 4,175 then 4,155 need to hold; resistance 4,221–4,227. September CPI (Wed Oct 14, 8:30 AM ET) is the main test.

items.title_en: China buys gold for a 23rd straight month: about 23 tonnes added in September
items.summary_en: Reuters: the People's Bank of China's gold reserves rose to 77.47M oz at end-September from 76.73M oz at end-August – an addition of 740,000 oz (≈ 23 tonnes), more than in August – extending the buying streak to 23 months. The value of its gold reserves fell from $350.08B to $323.52B as gold dropped more than 6% in September.
items.reason_en: Steady central-bank buying even into weakness puts a floor under gold at lower prices, though the dollar and yields still drive the short term.

items.title: Fed Hammack: cần chính sách thắt chặt hơn, tăng lãi suất 'từng bước nhỏ nhưng nhanh'
items.summary: Chủ tịch Fed Cleveland Beth Hammack (thành viên bỏ phiếu FOMC 2026) phát biểu tại hội nghị NABE ngày 12/10: 'lập trường chính sách thắt chặt là phù hợp' để đưa lạm phát về 2%, và bà muốn 'điều chỉnh nhỏ, làm tương đối nhanh' thay vì chờ rồi phải sửa sai mạnh hơn. Bà cảnh báo lạm phát cao kéo dài làm tăng nguy cơ 'tâm lý lạm phát' bám rễ; PCE tháng 8 ở 3,4%, PCE lõi 3%. Theo CME FedWatch (CNBC dẫn), thị trường thấy hơn 78% khả năng Fed giữ lãi suất trong tháng 10 nhưng gần 88% khả năng tăng vào tháng 12.
items.reason: Giọng điệu 'diều hâu' củng cố kỳ vọng Fed tăng lãi suất tiếp → lợi suất và USD được hỗ trợ, tăng chi phí cơ hội nắm giữ vàng. Áp lực có thể mạnh thêm nếu CPI thứ Tư 14/10 (19:30 giờ VN) cao hơn dự báo.

items.title_en: Fed's Hammack: policy needs to be tighter – hike in 'small but quick steps'
items.summary_en: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack (a 2026 FOMC voter) told the NABE conference on Oct 12 that 'a restrictive policy stance is appropriate' to get inflation back to 2%, and she favors 'small adjustments, made relatively quickly' rather than waiting and having to correct harder later. She warned persistent high inflation raises the risk of an inflation psychology taking hold; August PCE was 3.4%, core PCE 3%. Per CME FedWatch (cited by CNBC), the market sees over 78% odds of an October hold but nearly 88% odds of a December hike.
items.reason_en: A hawkish tone reinforces expectations of more Fed hikes → supports yields and the dollar, raising the opportunity cost of holding gold. Pressure could build if Wednesday's CPI (Oct 14, 8:30 AM ET) comes in hot.
items.time_en: CNBC posted Oct 12, 1:08 PM ET

items.title: Iran tấn công thêm siêu tàu dầu ở Hormuz; USD gần đỉnh 18 tháng, vàng mất mốc 4.200 USD
items.summary: Hải quân Vệ binh Cách mạng Iran (IRGC) cho biết sáng thứ Hai 12/10 đã đánh trúng một siêu tàu dầu cố đi qua eo biển Hormuz khi tắt bộ phát tín hiệu, khiến tàu bốc cháy (AFP) – vụ thứ 3 trong 2 ngày theo IRGC. Thị trường trái phiếu Mỹ nghỉ lễ Columbus Day.
items.reason: Rủi ro chiến sự hỗ trợ nhu cầu trú ẩn, nhưng dầu cao giữ lạm phát cao → kỳ vọng Fed tăng lãi suất (khoảng 85% khả năng tăng trước tháng 12 theo Kitco) và USD mạnh đang lấn át – vàng chịu sức ép trước CPI.

items.title_en: Iran hits another supertanker in Hormuz; dollar near 18-month high, gold loses $4,200

Kitco: spot gold briefly topped $4,200 in Asian trade before slipping to about $4,156 ahead of the New York open (down nearly 1%); DXY around 102.2, near its highest in about 18 months; Brent around $105, WTI above $92/bbl. The Treasury market was closed for Columbus Day.
items.reason_en: War risk supports safe-haven demand, but high oil keeps inflation elevated → Fed hike expectations (about 85% odds of a hike by December per Kitco) and a strong dollar are winning out – gold under pressure ahead of CPI.

items.summary_en: On Monday Oct 12 gold gave up its early gains as crude rose and US diesel recovered (after a 3% drop Friday to $4.74/gal), even though President Trump eased sanctions on Russian diesel and announced a Russia–Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'. Fears of a wider conflict grew after the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh airport and two Saudi Aramco facilities; Trump suggested the US could join Saudi Arabia in striking the Houthis.
items.reason_en: The 'oil → inflation → rates' channel: Middle East tension lifts crude and reinforces the case for Fed hikes – bearish for gold. Heraeus: 'gold remains under pressure as Middle East tensions keep pushing oil prices higher'.
